heading: Wednesday, October 15, 2025
topLine: Gemma-based single-cell model predicts a drug combination that boosts tumour antigen presentation. Also: 2 model releases: Anthropic Claude Haiku 4.5 and Google Veo 3.1.

items.headline: Gemma-based single-cell model predicts a drug combination that boosts tumour antigen presentation
items.summary: Google and Yale's 27-billion-parameter Cell2Sentence-Scale model predicted that the CK2 inhibitor silmitasertib would raise MHC-I antigen presentation only in an immune-context-positive setting, a link not previously reported. Yale experiments in human neuroendocrine cell models unseen in training found silmitasertib alone had no effect but combined with low-dose interferon produced about a 50% increase; reported in a company blog post and a bioRxiv preprint, needing further preclinical work.

items.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Haiku 4.5
items.summary: Claude Haiku 4.5 is Anthropic's small model. Anthropic says it matches Claude Sonnet 4 on coding at about one-third the cost and more than twice the speed, and reports 73.3% on SWE-bench Verified. It is priced at $1/$5 per million input/output tokens.

items.headline: Google releases Veo 3.1 video model
items.summary: Veo 3.1 builds on Veo 3 with stronger prompt adherence and better audiovisual quality, and it brings audio to Flow features such as Ingredients to Video and Extend. It is available in Flow, the Gemini app, the Gemini API and Vertex AI.
